text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.

- Crop harvests in southern African countries, including Zambia, are likely to fall by 20 percent because of climatic pattern in the region, the United Nations inter-governmental panel on climate says in a publication.

- Lawyers representing opposition parties seeking a stay of the November 18 elections have refused to have their case heard by the deputy chief justice Bonaventure Bweupe because he is purportedly partisan towards the ruling Movement for Multi-party emocracy.

- Police have arrested a school headmaster for pulling down a campaign poster of president Frederick Chiluba from his school and will charge him with a breach of the peace. The headmaster said he pulled down the poster because the school would be used as a polling station in the November 18 elections. Campaign posters are not allowed at polling stations.
- The Bank of Zambia may collapse following a ruling by a British court that it pay Camdex, a company based in the Bahamas, $120 million for failing to service a debt.
